validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE: strongly confirmed, real and FERC-certificated, NOT a GEM-only entity. FERC docket CP17-26 (filed by Pomelo Connector, LLC on 12/23/16, joined to the related Texas Eastern Transmission South Texas Expansion docket CP15-499) is documented independently in: the Federal Register's own notice (federalregister.gov/documents/2017/08/23/2017-17847, 'Pomelo Connector, LLC, Texas Eastern Transmission, LP; Notice of Schedule for Environmental Review of the Pomelo Connector Pipeline and South Texas Expansion Projects', docket nos. CP17-26-000/CP15-499-000/-001 — read live, not just the wiki's dead casetext.com mirror of the same notice, which 410s); a FERC-pending-projects compilation (marcellusdrilling.com PDF, table row 'CP17-26 Pomelo Connector, LLC Pomelo Connector Pipeline (see CP15-499-001) 400 [MMcf/d] 14 [mi] 5,000.00 [HP] TX 12/23/16' — confirmed by pdftotext -layout since the automated verifier's substring check false-negatives on this PDF's compressed text stream, a known limitation for PDF content checks, not a live/dead signal); Natural Gas Intelligence trade-press coverage of FERC's construction certificate (naturalgasintel.com, Feb 15 2018, David Bradley); Pipeline & Gas Journal's Oct-2018 'Ongoing Projects' compilation (s3.amazonaws.com/pgj-wp-media PDF, dedicated POMELO CONNECTOR LLC entry with owner/length/diameter/location/capacity/comments, same PDF-compression verifier caveat as above); the developer's own project page (canyonmidstream.com/projects/pomelo-connector-llc); and SEC filings (Spectra Energy Partners 8-K, 5/9/2018, announcing construction start; Enbridge Inc.'s FY2017-FY2025 10-Ks, which list 'Pomelo Connector, LLC' as a Delaware subsidiary every year running). This is five-plus independent origins (government notice, government-filing compilation, two separate trade-press outlets, the original developer, and the current parent's own audited SEC filings) all describing the same 14-mile, 30-inch, Nueces-County pipeline connecting Tetco to Valley Crossing. CLASSIFICATION: correct as a gas transmission connector — it is an interstate, FERC-jurisdictional pipe (not a gathering/feeder line) built specifically to move firm transportation capacity between Texas Eastern Transmission's system and the Valley Crossing Pipeline (P0276) for eventual export to Mexico via the Sur de Texas-Tuxpan system (P0257); Fuel=Gas is unambiguous in every source. DUPLICATE: checked against all 44 other roster rows — this is a short (14 mi) interconnector distinct from Valley Crossing Pipeline (P0276, 171 mi, the larger pipe it feeds into) and from Texas Eastern Transmission itself; no other row describes this Petronila-to-Agua Dulce corridor or cites the CP17-26 docket. No merge/relabel indicated. COVERAGE: opened 8 of the 10 harvested wiki citations for this row (all but spglobal.com and seekingalpha.com, both of which 403 on every fetch path tried — curl with a browser UA, WebFetch, and the verifier — and are therefore left as blocked-not-deleted, never cited); the two I could read in full (NGI, Canyon Midstream) plus my own SEC EDGAR full-text search (efts.sec.gov, 'Pomelo Connector' phrase match) supplied everything below. fractracker.org and eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php are both live but generic (neither names Pomelo) and are not cited for any value.

validity.recommendation: Change StartYear1 from 2019 to 2018 (Q4). Two of Enbridge/Spectra Energy Partners' own SEC filings put the Pomelo Connector's in-service date in the fourth quarter of 2018, not 2019: the Q3-2018 earnings release (Nov 2, 2018) states 'the South Texas Expansion Project (STEP) and the Pomelo Connector are both on track for an in-service date in the fourth quarter 2018', and the audited FY2018 10-K (filed 2/15/2019) confirms in its capex-by-project footnotes that 'the...South Texas Expansion Project and Pomelo Connector Pipeline Project [were] placed into service in the fourth quarter of 2018.' I could not find a second, non-Enbridge origin restating the exact quarter, so I'm calling this a documented concern rather than a silent correction — but an audited 10-K stating an asset was placed in service is about as authoritative as a start-date source gets, and nothing found anywhere (including the harvested pool) supports 2019.
validity.researcher_notes: Sources: SEC EDGAR full-text search for 'Pomelo' turned up Spectra Energy Partners LP's Q3 2018 earnings 8-K exhibit (filed 11/2/2018) and Enbridge Inc.'s FY2018 10-K (filed 2/15/2019, main document). Both are the operating company's own reporting (same corporate family across two document types, one a press release and one an audited annual report), so I'm treating this as one strong origin rather than two fully independent ones — hence tier=medium rather than high, though I have high confidence in the fact itself given the specificity and audited nature of the second source.

validity.recommendation: Flag SegmentCost=$130,000,000 for a second look rather than replacing it — leaving it as-is pending clarification of what SEP's $260M figure actually represents (construction-only vs. all-in acquisition+construction).
validity.researcher_notes: SEP's own 8-K (5/9/2018) states: 'In December 2017, SEP acquired Pomelo Connector LLC...In April 2018, SEP commenced construction on the Pomelo Connector, a 14-mile pipeline that will provide 400,000 dth/d...The total project capex, including acquisition cost, is $260 million.' That $260M figure is roughly DOUBLE the sheet's SegmentCost of $130M, but the phrase 'including acquisition cost' means it is not a clean apples-to-apples comparison against a construction-cost-only SegmentCost field — GEM's $130M could plausibly represent just the pipe/compressor-station capex, with the other ~$130M being the M&A premium SEP paid Canyon Midstream Partners for the already-FERC-certificated development company (a wiki-cited S&P Global headline, 'FERC approves $137M Enbridge project,' is in the right range for a construction-only figure but I could not read the article itself — spglobal.com 403s on every fetch path — so I'm not citing it, only noting the number is consistent). I did not find any source that states a $130M (or similarly construction-only) figure directly, so I'm not proposing this as a confirmed value; it's flagged for a researcher to resolve which quantity SegmentCost is meant to capture, not silently left alone.

fills.researcher_notes: Enbridge's audited FY2018 10-K states the Pomelo Connector was 'placed into service in the fourth quarter of 2018' (i.e. operating status inferred by context, per convention — a placed-in-service asset is operating); NGI's Feb-2018 article separately describes FERC's construction certificate and the abandon/lease order transferring the built capacity to Tetco. Two different-type, non-restated sources both consistent with an in-service, operating pipeline.
SEP's 8-K describes it as a 'natural gas pipeline project'; NGI describes it moving natural gas exports to Mexico. Unambiguous.

NGI ('30-inch diameter'), the developer's own page ('30" pipeline'), and Pipeline & Gas Journal's Oct-2018 project listing ('Diameter: 30 inches') all agree; no conflicting figure found anywhere.
